sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Mundelein, Illinois?
sections.html:
Mundelein is a Lake County village about 33 miles northwest of the Chicago Loop, and a sale there runs through the Lake County Clerk's recording division in Waukegan. Sellers usually weigh an agent listing, a sale by owner, and a direct sale to a cash buyer who takes the house as is.

The village straddles Libertyville and Fremont townships and borders Grayslake, Ivanhoe, Diamond Lake, Libertyville, Hawthorn Woods and Vernon Hills. Its housing stock reflects its growth: ranches and tri-levels were built in the center of town in the 1950s and 1960s, and larger two-story houses followed on the edges from the 1970s.

That mix matters for pricing. A tri-level near the old center and a newer two-story near the village edge attract different buyers, and the repair needs are different too.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Mundelein?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau counted 31,560 residents in 2020 and estimates 32,680 for July 2025, up 3.5 percent from the 2020 base. The village has 9.59 square miles of land and about 3,293 people per square mile.

For 2020 to 2024, median owner-occupied value is $309,700 and median gross rent is $1,566. Owners occupy 71.2 percent of housing units across 11,632 households averaging 2.72 people. Median household income is $108,340, and the mean commute is 27.9 minutes.

  • At 2.72 people per household, buyers may look hard at bedroom count and basement space.
  • About 34.6 percent of residents are Hispanic or Latino and 45.1 percent speak a language other than English at home, so bilingual listing materials reach more buyers.
  • Growth is steady, with the Census estimate above the 2020 count.

sections.h2: How did Mundelein grow, and why does it matter to a seller?
sections.html:
The area was first settled by Europeans in 1835. The village went through several names: Mechanics Grove, Holcomb, Rockefeller and Area, before it adopted Mundelein in 1925 in honor of the Chicago cardinal. It was incorporated in 1909, after a spur line of the Chicago North Shore and Milwaukee Railroad reached the village.

The University of Saint Mary of the Lake opened in 1921 on the former Sheldon School estate, and in June 1926 the village hosted the closing events of the 28th International Eucharistic Congress. Ball Glass, a major employer, closed in the early 1980s, and the village added more than 10,000 residents between the 1980 and 1990 censuses.

A recent expansion is the 2022 annexation of more than 700 acres of land owned by the Wirtz family, where the plan was to build 1,200 houses and 600 townhomes. New construction near your house is competition to watch, so price against what buyers can find new as well as resale houses.

sections.h2: Which schools, roads and trains serve Mundelein?
sections.html:
Mundelein is served by five elementary districts, which means the district for your street varies. They are Diamond Lake School District 76, Fremont School District 79, Hawthorn Community Consolidated School District 73, Libertyville School District 70 and Mundelein Elementary School District 75. Mundelein High School serves the village, and Carmel High School and the University of Saint Mary of the Lake are private institutions in town.

  • Rail: Metra's North Central Service stops in Mundelein with weekday service between Antioch and Chicago Union Station. The station opened in 1996.
  • Bus: Pace Route 574 links Mundelein with Grayslake, Vernon Hills and other stops.
  • Streets: Lake Street, Illinois Route 60, Illinois Route 83, Maple Avenue, Midlothian Road and Hawley Street carry most traffic.
  • Interstate: Interstate 94 is five miles east.

The village hall opened in 2014 on a 10-acre site next to the Metra station, which puts the civic center and the train in the same place. Homes within walking distance of that area are easy to market on convenience.

sections.h2: Does Diamond Lake or the weather change how a Mundelein house sells?
sections.html:
Diamond Lake is a 153-acre glacial lake in south Mundelein, used for fishing, swimming and boating, and it drains to the Des Plaines River. Homes near it may appeal to buyers who want water access, and a lakefront or creekside lot should prompt you to confirm flood zone status before you list.

The village has a flood history. Floods in September 1936 and June 1937 damaged the main road and nearby businesses and neighborhoods. Disclose any water events at your own address on the seller report.

Mundelein has a humid continental climate with warm to hot summers and cold winters. Since 1999 the record high was 103 degrees in July 2012 and the record low was 26 below zero in January 2019. Buyers inspecting a house will check the roof, furnace and sump pump in light of swings like that.

sections.h2: What do Mundelein's building and permit offices require?
sections.html:
The Village of Mundelein posts a Permit Application for building and property work or new construction, plus a Homeowner Project Guide, and online fee payments. Contact customer service at 847-949-3283 or building@mundelein.org about a specific project. The main village line is 847-949-3200.

Before listing, collect permit records for any addition, deck, roof, furnace or finished basement. A buyer's inspector will compare the house to the permit history, and a missing permit is easier to resolve before an offer than during the buyer's inspection period.

The village also provides water delivery and wastewater treatment, from a Lake Michigan supply. Ask the village about final water billing so the account closes at your sale date.

sections.h2: How is a deed recorded in Lake County, and are there extra transfer taxes?
sections.html:
The Lake County Clerk's Recording Division is at 18 N County Street, 6th Floor, Waukegan, and its number is 847-377-2575. Its fee page lists a standard document at $70 and a non-standard document at $82, and says the only additional fees at recording are the state and county real estate transfer taxes.

Illinois sets the state tax at 50 cents per $500 of value in 35 ILCS 200/31-15. The county eRecording page names six municipalities that require municipal transfer tax stamps or a signed exemption certificate: Buffalo Grove, Highland Park, Lake Forest, Lincolnshire, Mettawa and North Chicago. Mundelein is not on that list. Deeds with a paper PTAX-203 cannot go through eRecording, and most deeds are eligible for it.

sections.h2: What should you prepare before accepting an offer in Mundelein?
sections.html:
Complete the statutory disclosure report first. Under 765 ILCS 77/20 the seller must fill in every item and give the report to the buyer before the contract is signed.

Then assemble the closing file: the parcel number, a current tax bill, any mortgage payoff statement, permit records, and the Mundelein water account details. Compare offers by net proceeds and by the number of contingencies, since a contingent offer can fall apart late.

A direct cash buyer can often close in a short window and takes the house as it stands. A listing can bring a higher price but takes longer. Match the route to your deadline.

faqs.q: Does Mundelein charge a municipal real estate transfer tax?
faqs.a: Mundelein is not among the six municipalities the Lake County Clerk lists as requiring municipal transfer stamps or an exemption certificate: Buffalo Grove, Highland Park, Lake Forest, Lincolnshire, Mettawa and North Chicago. The state tax of 50 cents per $500 still applies.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Mundelein house?
faqs.a: With the Lake County Clerk's Recording Division at 18 N County Street, 6th Floor, Waukegan, or through eRecording by an approved submitter. The phone number is 847-377-2575.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Lake County?
faqs.a: The Clerk's fee page lists a standard document at $70 and a non-standard document at $82, and says the only additional fees charged at recording are the state and county transfer taxes.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Mundelein house in?
faqs.a: Five elementary districts serve the village: Diamond Lake District 76, Fremont District 79, Hawthorn CCSD 73, Libertyville District 70 and Mundelein Elementary District 75. Mundelein High School serves the village for high school, so confirm the elementary district for your address.

faqs.q: How do I start a building permit in Mundelein?
faqs.a: Use the Permit Application and Homeowner Project Guide posted by the Village, and call customer service at 847-949-3283 or email building@mundelein.org with questions.
